title: Blood Pressure Cuff (Microgravity Protocol)
steps: Strap into a crew restraint and rest quietly for 5 minutes before inflating.
Position the cuffed upper arm cleanly at heart level (avoid floating elevation).
Take 2 consecutive readings spaced 1 minute apart and log the average systolic/diastolic values.
Compare against YOUR personal in-flight baseline (days 1–14), not Earth 120/80 norms.
why_it_matters: Microgravity cephalad fluid shift and reduced vascular resistance typically lower astronaut blood pressure by ~10 mmHg compared to pre-flight Earth baselines.
common_mistakes: Measuring immediately after ARED resistance exercise or floating upside-down.
Placing the cuff over thick flight-suit sleeves or below/above heart height.
Comparing single readings against Earth clinical cutoffs instead of in-flight personal baseline.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Re-wrap cuff snugly (two-finger slack), align artery marker over brachial artery, rest 5 minutes, and re-measure.
If readings differ by > 10 mmHg between attempts, take a 3rd reading after 2 minutes.

title: Wearable / Chest ECG & HRV Fit Check
steps: Moisten electrode contact pads lightly with water or conductive gel before strapping on.
Center the strap snugly below the pectoral line (or tighten wrist optical band 1 notch above the wrist bone).
Remain still for 60 seconds during spot checks or verify green signal-quality indicator (≥ 0.7) before sleep.
Sync buffered RR-interval / RMSSD data locally before morning review.
why_it_matters: HRV (RMSSD) and resting heart rate are our primary day-to-day autonomic stress and early infection signals (Mishra et al. 2020; Mehta et al. 2017).
common_mistakes: Loose wristband during sleep causing motion artifacts and fake HR > 200 bpm spikes.
Dry chest strap electrodes causing dropped beats (missing HRV / NaN).
Measuring HRV right after caffeine or exercise instead of resting morning window.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: When B.O.O.P.S. flags 'Check device', tighten strap contact, wipe optical sensor, and perform a 2-minute seated resting check.
If chest strap stays noisy, use the offline camera rPPG spot-check module as a cross-sensor confirmation.

title: Core / Oral Thermometer Guide
steps: Wait at least 15 minutes after hot drinks, cold water, or intense exercise before oral measurement.
Place probe under the posterior sublingual pocket and keep lips sealed until the steady tone.
If using infrared tympanic mode, pull ear gently upward/backward and aim at the eardrum.
Repeat once on the opposite side if reading is < 35.5 °C or ≥ 37.5 °C.
why_it_matters: Subtle temperature rises (+0.5–1.0 °C) combined with resting HR jumps distinguish true early infection from isolated sleep loss or stress.
common_mistakes: Cold probe air gap yielding implausible values (< 30 °C) flagged as Check device.
Measuring immediately after drinking cold pouch water.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Warm probe tip briefly in clean hand, reseal probe cover, and re-measure in the opposite sublingual pocket.
Cross-check resting HR and symptoms if temperature reads ≥ 37.5 °C.

title: Saliva Sample Kit (Cortisol & Viral Shedding)
steps: Collect immediately upon waking (before brushing teeth, eating, or drinking) for baseline cortisol rhythm.
Rinse mouth gently with potable water, wait 10 minutes, then saturate the Salivette cotton swab for 2 minutes without chewing excessively.
Seal tube, scan/log crew ID + mission day, and place in the onboard cold-stowage / biomarker reader slot.
Log collection timestamp and any oral sores or throat symptoms.
why_it_matters: Salivary cortisol, DHEA, and viral DNA shedding (EBV/HSV-1/VZV) directly confirm HPA-axis stress and latent virus reactivation before severe clinical symptoms appear.
common_mistakes: Collecting within 30 minutes of food, coffee, or toothpaste (contaminates assay).
Bleeding gums contaminating sample with serum cortisol.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Discard visually blood-tinted swabs, rinse mouth gently, wait 15 minutes, and repeat with a fresh swab.
Always pair a Watch/Act immune alert with a morning saliva test.

title: Personal Radiation Dosimeter Guide
steps: Wear active personal dosimeter clipped consistently to the chest flight pocket (never inside shielded lockers).
Read daily cumulative dose (mSv) at the same UTC time each day and log total mission + career cumulative mSv.
Verify comparison against NASA's 600 mSv career limit and check NOAA/module storm alarm state.
why_it_matters: Space radiation spikes during Solar Particle Events suppress lymphocytes and amplify bone resorption and oxidative stress.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dosimeter inside a sleeping berth or shielded water-wall area during normal shifts.
Confusing dose rate (µSv/h) with 24-hour cumulative dose (mSv).
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Compare personal dosimeter reading with the module area radiation monitor (RAM); if only one spikes, inspect battery/shielding placement.
During an active SPE alert, prioritize shelter move before manual logging.

title: Pulse Oximeter (SpO2) Guide
steps: Warm hands for 30 seconds (microgravity reduces peripheral fingertip perfusion if cabin is cool).
Clip sensor fully onto index or middle finger with nail facing upward; rest hand still for 20 seconds.
Wait for a steady pulse waveform bar before recording SpO2 (%) and pulse rate.
why_it_matters: SpO2 verifies respiratory oxygen delivery and serves as an independent cross-sensor check against wrist optical heart rate.
common_mistakes: Cold fingers or motion causing false SpO2 < 85% drops.
Ambient cabin glare hitting an unshielded sensor.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Warm fingers, switch to another finger, shield sensor from direct LED cabin light, and verify pulse waveform matches manual radial pulse.
If SpO2 stays < 92% with shortness of breath or high CO2, launch the Breathing Difficulty emergency protocol immediately.

title: ARED / CEVIS / T2 Exercise Countermeasure Log
steps: Log total aerobic + resistive exercise minutes and separate ARED resistance minutes after each session.
Record load settings, number of completed sets, and mark EVA days (eva = 1) accurately.
Aim for ≥ 120 total exercise min/day including ~60 min ARED mechanical loading.
why_it_matters: Exercise offsets cardiac atrophy and bone/muscle unloading; skipping resistance training interacts multiplicatively with stress cortisol to accelerate muscle loss.
common_mistakes: Logging aerobic CEVIS cycling as resistance loading (does not load lumbar spine/femur sufficiently).
Forgetting to mark an EVA day, causing post-EVA RHR/HRV shifts to look like unexplained illness.
how_to_fix_bad_reading: Reconcile manual log with ARED / CEVIS onboard counter files at end of crew day.
Mark EVA = 1 for every spacewalk day so the infection early-warning filter accounts for EVA load.
